parts.label: a
parts.technique: Calculating Swt and Stt (regression/correlation summary statistics)
parts.reason: This is preparatory calculation for regression/correlation; S2.2 explicitly excludes 'calculations involving regression lines' and these sums (Swt, Stt) exist solely to compute regression coefficients and PMCC, which are excluded topics.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Sss, Sst summary statistics for regression
parts.reason: Same as (a); these values feed directly into the excluded regression line calculation (S2.2 exclusion) and PMCC (S5.1 exclusion).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Product moment correlation coefficient calculation via formula
parts.reason: S5.1 explicit exclusion: 'calculation of correlation coefficients is excluded' and 'use of the formula is not required'; here the formula is required.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Interpreting PMCC value
parts.reason: Depends entirely on the value of r computed in the excluded part (c); a part that only makes sense after an out-of-spec part is OUT.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Regression line equation (w on t)
parts.reason: S2.2 explicit exclusion: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Regression line equation (s on t) via coding
parts.reason: Same explicit S2.2 exclusion on regression line calculations; also depends on (e).

parts.label: g
parts.technique: Interpretation of regression coefficient
parts.reason: Depends on the regression line found in the excluded part (f), so it is OUT.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Histogram bar width/height from frequency density
parts.reason: S2.1 covers histograms and states area represents frequency; calculating width/height from frequency density is standard histogram work.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Linear interpolation for median from grouped data
parts.reason: S2.3 guidance explicitly expects 'use of linear interpolation to calculate percentiles from grouped data'.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Estimating mean from grouped frequency table
parts.reason: S2.3 covers measures of central tendency including mean for grouped/continuous data.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Estimating standard deviation from grouped data using Sxx
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculation of standard deviation including from summary statistics such as fy^2.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Describing skewness from mean/median comparison
parts.reason: S2.3 covers measures of central tendency and variation and expects students to 'draw simple inferences and give interpretations'; comparing mean and median to describe skewness fits this depth.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Commenting on suitability of Normal model based on skewness
parts.reason: S4.3 explicitly requires selecting/critiquing whether Normal model is appropriate, with reasoning based on distribution shape.

parts.label: g
parts.technique: Finding a percentile using the Normal distribution (inverse standardisation)
parts.reason: S4.2 covers using the Normal distribution to find probabilities/values (including via calculator), no derivation or pdf knowledge required, matching this problem.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Independent events probability calculation (Venn diagram)
parts.reason: S3.1 covers independent events and use of P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) with Venn diagrams.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Venn diagram probability using total probability =1
parts.reason: S3.2 covers Venn diagrams and probability rules such as P(A')=1-P(A) style calculations.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Further Venn diagram region probabilities
parts.reason: Continuation of standard Venn diagram probability work covered by S3.1/S3.2.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Testing independence of events A and B
parts.reason: S3.1 explicitly covers use of P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) to test/establish independence.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Conditional probability P(B|A∪C)
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly covers conditional probability formula P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B), extendable to compound events using Venn diagram regions.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding probabilities and CDF values for a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 covers 'simple, discrete probability distributions' generally (not just binomial), and this only involves probabilities summing to 1 and cumulative distribution function values, not mean/variance which is the only explicit exclusion.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Reading a probability from a distribution (P(X^2=1))
parts.reason: Simple probability lookup from the distribution table found in (a); covered by S4.1/S3.1 basic probability work.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Standardising and finding a Normal probability
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution via standardisation and calculator.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Conditional probability with Normal distribution
parts.reason: Combines S3.2 conditional probability formula with S4.2 Normal probabilities; no CLT or pdf knowledge required.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Finding an unknown value from conditional Normal probability = 0.5 (inverse standardisation)
parts.reason: Uses S4.2 Normal distribution (calculator-based, no pdf/derivation) combined with S3.2 conditional probability; matches depth of statements.

parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion: 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables is excluded'.

parts.label: b

parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion covers variance of discrete random variables directly.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Forming linear equation from E(Y)=3 to find p
parts.reason: Requires using E(Y), the mean of a discrete random variable, which S4.1 explicitly excludes; the whole method depends on this excluded concept.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Writing probability distribution of Y using p found in (c)
parts.reason: Depends directly on the value of p obtained in the out-of-spec part (c) (which used excluded E(Y)); a part only making sense after an out-of-spec part is OUT.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Calculating P(S=30) via P(X=6)×P(Y=5) using independent events
parts.reason: Although the technique of multiplying probabilities of independent events (S3.1) is itself in spec, this value only makes sense using P(Y=5)=p from the probability distribution of Y established in the out-of-spec parts (c) and (d); a part that only makes sense after an out-of-spec part is OUT.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Constructing probability distribution of S=XY (or Y^2)
parts.reason: Depends on the probability distribution of Y from the out-of-spec parts (c)/(d), so this part is OUT.

parts.label: g
parts.technique: E(S) of a general discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion of mean of discrete random variables applies directly to E(S).

parts.technique: Comparing E(X^2) and E(S) to decide higher total score
parts.reason: Requires E(X^2) and E(S), both means of discrete random variables, explicitly excluded by S4.1.
